events.label: Guardian-TBIJ investigation of illegal children’s homes in England

slots.name: annual spending
slots.sentence: Councils are paying more than £125m a year of taxpayers’ money to place vulnerable children in illegal care homes across England, an investigation has found.

slots.name: private companies
slots.sentence: Local authority payment records show that more than 480 private companies have been paid £250m for 1,800 unlawful placements of children over the past two years.

slots.name: illegal homes identified
slots.sentence: Unregistered care has expanded rapidly in recent years, with Ofsted identifying 710 illegal homes this year, up from 144 in 2020.

slots.name: 28-day limit
slots.sentence: The Guardian has identified at least 11 companies offering 28-day breaks.

slots.name: DMC payment
slots.sentence: Thurrock council paid DMC Consulting Services £2.7m for two children in a two-year illegal placement.

slots.name: safeguarding allegations
slots.sentence: In total, there were 44 allegations that staff had harmed or posed a risk to children between January 2024 and April 2026.

slots.name: placement earnings
slots.sentence: Average earnings of more than £150,000 per placement have attracted entrepreneurs from outside the care sector.

slots.name: Prospero offices
